review_candidates.description: Requisition Id 16982 Overview: The Field Intelligence Operations Division (FIOD) of the National Security Directorate (NSSD), is seeking an exceptional Linux Engineer to help design, build, and advance the secure computing environments behind some of the nation’s most consequential national security, intelligence, and scientific missions. You’ll have genuine ownership over mission-critical accounts and work closely with a small, focused team trusted to execute with minimal supervision. The position requires Top-Secret Clearance with access to Q and SCI. This is not a traditional Linux administration role. You will work at the intersection of advanced Linux engineering, cybersecurity, high-performance computing, emerging technologies, and classified mission systems—solving complex technical challenges in environments where security, reliability, and performance are critical. As a Linux Engineer, you will help architect, implement, automate, operate, and continuously modernize highly secure Linux infrastructure supporting both current missions and rapidly evolving capabilities. You will work across multiple security domains and collaborate with cybersecurity professionals, systems and network engineers, scientists, researchers, and mission partners to turn demanding requirements into resilient, scalable, and secure computing solutions. We are looking for someone who enjoys building, automating, troubleshooting, experimenting, and solving problems others cannot. The ideal candidate brings deep Linux expertise, a strong engineering mindset, curiosity about emerging technologies, and the drive to continually improve how secure computing environments are designed and operated. If you are a Linux engineer who wants more than routine administration—and you want to apply your skills to technically challenging problems with real national impact—this is an opportunity to build systems that matter. Major Duties/Responsibilities: Engineer and modernize secure Linux infrastructure supporting classified national security, intelligence, scientific, HPC, and emerging mission environments, primarily using Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) and related distributions. Design, build, configure, optimize, and sustain physical and virtual Linux platforms across multiple security domains. Develop automation using Ansible, Python, Bash, and Git-based workflows to improve deployment, configuration, patching, compliance, reliability, and operational efficiency. Implement cybersecurity requirements including RMF, NIST 800-53, STIGs, DOE directives, and ICD 503, including system hardening, vulnerability remediation, monitoring, and secure logging. Integrate Linux environments with enterprise identity, virtualization, storage, backup, and monitoring capabilities, including Active Directory, LDAP, Kerberos, PKI, VMware, and KVM. Troubleshoot complex technical issues and partner with cybersecurity, networking, storage, application, HPC, and mission teams to develop secure, scalable solutions. Evaluate and introduce new technologies, architectures, and engineering approaches that advance infrastructure modernization and emerging mission capabilities. Support mission-critical operations, planned maintenance, and occasional after-hours requirements. Basic Qualifications: BS degree in a related technical field and at least five years of Linux engineering or administration experience. Equivalent education, experience, and certifications may be considered. Current Top-Secret clearance with Q and SCI eligibility. Demonstrated expertise with RHEL/Linux engineering, troubleshooting, performance tuning, automation, and scripting. Experience with Ansible, Python, Bash, enterprise virtualization, identity integration, storage, monitoring/logging, and cybersecurity compliance. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to independently solve complex technical challenges and collaborate across multidisciplinary teams. Preferred Qualifications: Experience in one or more of the following: Classified, Intelligence Community, DoD, DOE, or other highly regulated computing environments. HPC, AI/ML infrastructure, GPU computing, containers, Kubernetes, or advanced computing platforms. Infrastructure-as-code, advanced automation, CI/CD, or enterprise configuration management. Enterprise virtualization, storage, backup, and disaster-recovery architectures. RMF, NIST 800-53, STIG implementation, vulnerability management, or authorization activities. Designing or modernizing enterprise Linux environments and introducing emerging technologies. Relevant Linux, automation, cybersecurity, virtualization, or cloud certifications. Security, Credentials, and Eligibility Requirements: Q clearance with SCI: This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance from the Department of Energy. WSAP positions require passing a pre-placement drug test and participation in an ongoing random drug testing program. In addition, due the SCI, you may also be subject to random polygraph testing. Our team is made up of over 7,000 dedicated and innovative individuals! Our goal is to create an environment where a variety of perspectives and backgrounds are valued, ensuring ORNL is known as a top choice for employment. These principles are essential for supporting our broader mission to drive scientific breakthroughs and translate them into solutions for energy, environmental, and security challenges facing the nation. ORNL offers competitive pay and benefits programs to attract and retain individuals who demonstrate exceptional work behaviors. The laboratory provides a range of employee benefits, including medical and retirement plans and flexible work hours, to support the well-being of you and your family. Employee amenities such as on-site fitness, banking, and cafeteria facilities are also available for added convenience. Other benefits include the following: Prescription Drug Plan, Dental Plan, Vision Plan, 401(k) Retirement Plan, Contributory Pension Plan, Life Insurance, Disability Benefits, Generous Vacation and Holidays, Parental Leave, Legal Insurance with Identity Theft Protection, Employee Assistance Plan, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, Wellness Programs, Educational Assistance, Relocation Assistance, and Employee Discounts. review_candidates.description: DevOps Engineer (Cloud Migration & Platform Engineering) A hands-on engineering role combining AWS migration work with platform and developer experience improvements on a newly won client engagement, fully remote, paying £60,000-£70,000. About the Company Our client is a global technology consultancy with a growing Cloud and DevOps practice based in Belfast, operating as part of their wider London delivery organisation. They have recently won a significant engagement with an energy trading business and are building the delivery team for it now. This is one of the first hires onto that engagement, and the role carries visibility at senior level within the business. The Role This is a broad DevOps role with two strands of work running alongside each other. The first is migration: moving an on-premise VMware estate onto AWS EC2, beginning with the logical test environment, which calls for genuine vSphere and ESXi depth rather than cloud experience alone. The second is platform: improving self-service tooling, CI/CD and the parts of the deployment process that currently leave engineers waiting. You would work embedded in the client's team day to day while being employed, paid and developed by the consultancy, with a manager in Belfast responsible for your progression and for your next engagement once this one completes. Key Responsibilities Migrate on-premise VMware workloads onto AWS EC2, starting with the logical test estate. Own CI/CD pipelines end to end, building and maintaining Azure DevOps YAML pipelines. Develop self-service tooling that removes the bottlenecks currently slowing developers down. Manage containerised workloads on EKS, authoring and maintaining Helm charts. Automate infrastructure provisioning and configuration through infrastructure as code. Administer Linux and Windows server estates across development, test and production. Build observability across the platform using tooling such as Grafana, Prometheus and Splunk. Work with security teams to embed container and Kubernetes security into the delivery process. Act as a visible technical point of contact for the client throughout the engagement. What You'll Need Essential: Experience in a DevOps, platform, infrastructure or build engineering role. Strong hands-on AWS experience, specifically EC2 and EKS. Demonstrable end-to-end ownership of CI/CD pipelines, ideally Azure DevOps with YAML. Hands-on VMware vSphere and ESXi administration, including migrating virtualised workloads. Helm chart authoring alongside practical day-to-day Kubernetes experience. Linux server administration and scripting in Bash and/or PowerShell. Desirable: Windows Server administration across a virtualised estate. Observability tooling including Splunk, Grafana or Prometheus, with experience building alerting rather than inheriting it. Container and Kubernetes security, including exposure to threat modelling. Infrastructure as code using Terraform, Ansible or equivalent. Previous experience in a consultancy or client-facing delivery environment. Exposure to energy, commodities or financial trading platforms. Relevant AWS certification. Why Apply? Fully remote with no routine office requirement. £60,000-£70,000 permanent. Joining at the very start of a newly won engagement that carries visibility at senior level. Genuine ownership of the developer experience rather than maintaining someone else's platform. A rare combination of traditional virtualisation and modern cloud work in a single role. Structured investment in certifications and progression between client engagements. Continuity of employment and pay between placements, which contracting does not offer. Interested? If this sounds like your next move, reach out to Jordan Madden at Ocho on LinkedIn for a confidential conversation.
